title: The repair district
question: Why does a repair miss its promised date?
summary: A promise crosses many hands. Follow an appliance from the customer's home to the workshop, and see how information and parts keep the work moving—or hold it up.

presentation.intro: Behind every repair is a neighborhood of people, places and dependencies.
presentation.caption: A world you can read, from the street to the server.

sources.title: Northbank Repair — example brief
sources.locator: brief.md · Operating rules and technical architecture

entities.label: Customer home
entities.description: Where the journey begins and where a missed promise is felt. The customer requests a repair, approves the quote and receives the returned appliance.
entities.constraint: A collection can only succeed when the supplied address is correct.

entities.label: Service desk
entities.description: The coordinator records the request, arranges collection, communicates the diagnosis and quote, and keeps the customer informed.
entities.constraint: A customer update depends on reliable status from the workshop and depot.

entities.label: Parts supplier
entities.description: Supplies a replacement part when the workshop's physical stock cannot cover a repair. Its delivery becomes a dependency of the waiting job.
entities.constraint: A supplier order is not the same as a part being available at the bench.

entities.label: Repair workshop
entities.description: The technician diagnoses the fault, checks the actual shelf, completes an approved repair and performs a quality check before release.
entities.constraint: The inventory record can say a part exists even when the physical shelf is empty.

entities.label: Delivery depot
entities.description: Connects the customer's home and the workshop. Collection, failed attempts, rescheduling and the final return are coordinated here.
entities.constraint: A failed collection prevents diagnosis from starting, even if workshop capacity is available.

entities.label: Booking
entities.description: Holds the customer-supplied address and collection window. An address correction must reach this record before the depot reschedules.
entities.constraint: The depot uses the address and collection window stored here to plan its run.

entities.label: Job records
entities.description: Records diagnosis, customer approval, work state and completion. It links coordination at the desk to activity at the workshop.
entities.constraint: A recorded job state must be kept consistent with what has actually happened.

entities.label: Inventory
entities.description: Supports stock checks. In the missing-part scenario, this record disagrees with the physical shelf and triggers an external order.
entities.constraint: Recorded availability does not guarantee physical availability.

entities.label: Supplier orders
entities.description: Carries a replacement-part request from the workshop to the supplier. Work remains dependent on the part arriving.
entities.constraint: Submitting an order does not mean the repair can resume.

entities.label: Dispatch
entities.description: Supports the depot's collection and return schedule. A corrected address creates a new collection attempt rather than erasing the failed one.
entities.constraint: Scheduling and successful collection are distinct events.

entities.label: Notifications
entities.description: Delivers messages from the service desk to the customer, including the explanation that a part is missing and a date needs revisiting.
entities.constraint: Communication makes a delay visible; it does not resolve the underlying dependency.

entities.label: Application servers
entities.description: Runs booking, job records, inventory and dispatch. These applications support the coordinator, technician and depot.
entities.constraint: The applications depend on this shared runtime and its connection to the operational database.

entities.label: Operational database
entities.description: Stores addresses, appointments, job state, recorded inventory and dispatch schedules. The application servers read and write these records.
entities.constraint: A working database can still contain an incorrect address or stock count; technical availability does not guarantee correct business information.

entities.label: Integration gateway
entities.description: Connects supplier ordering and customer notifications to external endpoints. The application servers submit exchanges through this gateway.
entities.constraint: Supplier orders and customer updates rely on the gateway's external connections.

relationships.label: Authorize repair or request a status update
Booking runs on the application servers
Job records runs on the application servers
Inventory runs on the application servers
Dispatch runs on the application servers
Supplier orders uses the integration gateway
Applications read and write operational records

scenarios.label: Book a repair
scenarios.summary: From the service desk to a stored record.
scenarios.condition: The customer brings a repair request to the desk. The coordinator can use the booking application and its database.
scenarios.outcome: The address and requested collection window are stored, ready for the depot to arrange collection.

steps.title: Describe the fault
steps.text: At the service desk, the customer explains the fault and supplies a collection address. The coordinator opens a repair request.

state.caption: Repair request at the service desk

steps.title: Register the booking
steps.text: The coordinator enters the address and requested collection window in Booking at the workstation.

steps.title: Run the booking application
steps.text: Booking runs on the shared application servers, alongside job records, inventory and dispatch.

state.caption: Booking uses the highlighted application servers

steps.title: Store the booking
steps.text: The application writes the address and collection window to the operational database. The depot can use the stored booking to arrange collection.

state.caption: Booking stored in the operational database

scenarios.label: Routine repair
scenarios.summary: The right information. The right part.
scenarios.condition: Correct address; the required part is physically in stock.
scenarios.outcome: The approved appliance is repaired, checked and returned.

steps.title: A repair is requested
steps.text: The customer contacts the desk. The coordinator records the address and arranges a collection with the depot.

steps.title: From home to the bench
steps.text: The driver collects the appliance and delivers it to the workshop. Diagnosis can now begin.

steps.title: Diagnosis and approval
steps.text: The technician records the diagnosis. The desk communicates the quote, obtains customer approval and authorizes repair.

steps.title: The part is on the shelf
steps.text: The technician checks the stock record against the shelf. The required part is present, so the approved repair and quality check can be completed.

steps.title: A completed promise
steps.text: The workshop releases the checked appliance to the depot. The driver returns it to the customer.

scenarios.label: Missing part
scenarios.summary: A small mismatch. A much longer journey.
scenarios.condition: Collection and quote approval have succeeded; recorded stock differs from the physical shelf.
scenarios.outcome: The job waits for supply. It resumes after the replacement part arrives, then is repaired and returned.

steps.title: The shelf tells a different story
steps.text: After collection, diagnosis and approval, the technician discovers that a recorded part is absent. The completion promise now depends on replenishment.

steps.title: The repair becomes a waiting job
steps.text: The workshop requests the part through supplier ordering. Submitting the order does not make the part available: work waits on fulfillment.

steps.title: The delay reaches the customer
steps.text: The workshop reports the wait. The desk sends an update explaining the missing part; no new completion date is asserted before supply is confirmed.

steps.title: An extra coordination cycle
steps.text: The customer asks for progress. The desk checks with the workshop and passes the update back to the customer.

steps.title: A part, then a completed repair
steps.text: The replacement arrives. The technician completes the approved repair and quality check, updates the job, and releases it for return.

scenarios.label: Missed collection
scenarios.summary: The repair cannot start without the appliance.
scenarios.condition: The initial collection address is incorrect; the required part will be available once the appliance reaches the workshop.
scenarios.outcome: A corrected record enables a new collection. The ordinary approved repair and return sequence then completes.

steps.title: An incorrect address travels downstream
steps.text: The customer requests a repair. The desk records the supplied address and arranges collection; dispatch schedules the attempt.

steps.title: Collection fails
steps.text: The driver cannot collect at the incorrect address. The depot reports the failed attempt to the desk. No appliance has reached the workshop.

steps.title: Correct the source record
steps.text: The desk asks for a correction through a customer update. The customer supplies it, and the desk updates booking before arranging another attempt.

steps.title: A new collection succeeds
steps.text: The desk and depot reschedule using the corrected address. The driver collects the appliance and delivers it to the workshop.

steps.title: Resume the ordinary repair
steps.text: Diagnosis and quote approval now take place. With the part available, the technician repairs and checks the appliance before releasing it for return.
